G02.summary: Accepted with its defect owned rather than retired. Gate: 'Fresh catalog coverage or authorization_blocked with named next action'. Authorization was granted and the run performed on 9d1470f86. Catalog tier across 10 providers: 7 pass (claude 11, openai 9, cursor 28, antigravity 24, deepseek 2, minimax 8, zai 8). Gemini and copilot are not signed in and carry the named next action 'jcode login --provider', which is the gate's own alternative rather than a failure. Perplexity returned HTTP 404 on the live model catalog, and that is a real defect in this repository, not a provider outage: the catalog URL is built as {api_base}/models at openrouter-runtime lib.rs:543 while perplexity's api_base carries no /v1. Re-derived at acceptance time WITH a bearer attached, because an unauthenticated 404 can be a missing-credential shape rather than a routing fact: GET /models 404 with and without a key, GET /v1/models 401 invalid_api_key, POST /chat/completions 401, POST /v1/chat/completions 404. The routes are genuinely inverted, so appending /v1 to api_base would fix the catalog and break chat. That probe also corrected one of my own readings: gemini-api first looked like a second instance at 404, but with a bearer it returns 400 'Please pass a valid API key', which is Google's missing-credential shape and not a defect. Across all 6 profiles whose api_base lacks /v1, perplexity is the only inversion. The repair is owned by G02-FIX-1 (merged 36639e43e), injected before this acceptance under EXECUTION_PROTOCOL section 5 so that accepting this node does not orphan the only record of the defect. Full spending tier passes on claude (13/13, 4 calls, 2188 tokens) and through the Bifrost gateway on bridge/gpt-5.5 (12/12, 3 calls, 1018 tokens), with the gateway leg controlled by a closed-port base that fails the catalog check after an uncontrolled first attempt was traced to a persisted openai-compatible.env.

R09.summary: Both halves of the stall were the program's defect shape: the cache reported 'stale' about an entry that was still valid, and the client reported 'unavailable' for a session that was merely slow. Measured rather than reasoned: n=96 [TIMING] model_routes samples give p50 3185ms against a fixed 3s TTL, so 59.4% of builds outlived the cache entry that held them; steady state was build 3.2s, cache 3s, expire, rebuild. Fix: routes_memo_ttl() is now derived from OBSERVED_MAX_ROUTES_BUILD_MS times 3, clamped 30s..600s, so the TTL follows what builds actually cost on this machine; the single-flight lock became try_lock, serving a generation-current entry on WouldBlock so no caller queues behind an in-flight build; only the first build in a process still blocks, which is the one case with no honest alternative. Generation invalidation still governs correctness, so serving during a build is safe. The watchdog stops advising /restart for a connected-but-slow session, keyed on HistoryRecoveryState::last_send_ok, which proves the socket is alive. Both files were extracted into new modules because the oversized-file ratchet caught the growth and the file was split rather than re-baselined. Four gates, three with controls observed failing; gate 2's first version PASSED with the fix reverted and proved nothing (a TTL-fresh priming entry meant the test never reached the lock), which is the third worthless test of mine caught by requiring the control to fail first. jcode-base --lib 1230 passed, jcode-tui --lib 1884 passed. NOT VERIFIED: no live remote-session reproduction, and a hung-but-writable server would still be told 'no need to restart'.
